Librogame.title: Viperblood
Librogame.author: Luke Simonds
Librogame.Blurb:
The king is dying, and the only cure is a green water that runs somewhere under the crypt of the ancient queens. You are the next volunteer sent down to fetch it — the ones before you did not come back, though their notes did.
Fifteen rooms of jade and cold air, a statue you have to climb through, rabets who trade and ambush in equal measure, and a purple snake asleep on a pile of coin. Everything you carry out is yours to keep, if you carry yourself out with it.

Changes.Change: Rewritten for this engine: rooms that the original repeated in different states are single scenes that change with what you have done
"Return to your previous entry" replaced by explicit exits, and some entries became items or actions
DEATH & TREASURE is not used: fights, tests and damage were re-tuned for this engine
Enemy morale is not implemented; the chance of a random encounter is a rule we added
Abilities renamed Toughness, Agility, Strength, Instinct, and tests the original left open were assigned by us
Poison strikes once instead of over hours: this engine has no clock
The west door of the sleeping snake room leads to the pyre room, correcting a contradiction in the original
Original illustrations and map not included: they are not licensed with the text

Skill.name: Toughness
Skill.description: How much poison, gas and exhaustion you can take.

Skill.name: Agility
Skill.description: Squeezing through tight places, slipping past what is watching.

Skill.name: Strength
Skill.description: Shifting stone, forcing what will not move.

Skill.name: Instinct
Skill.description: Noticing what is out of place, reading a room before it reads you.

Variable.name: You know your way through the web
The web has already been sprung
The bottle is full of viperblood
Which side of the statue you crossed from
Which bank of the river you stand on

Page.Title: The stair of weathered jade
Page.Text:
VIPERBLOOD, an emerald green water rumoured to be found only in the First Crypt, is said to cure anything that afflicts humankind. The king is deathly ill. One at a time he is sending out "volunteers" from his court to retrieve some for him. It is your turn now. Any treasure you find is yours to keep as a reward for your service.
You have been equipped with a magic scroll on which you can write notes about what you find and record a map of the crypt. It returns to the castle upon the death of its bearer. It already carries a map, and the notes left by previous "volunteers".
Guards escort you to the ancient burial grounds. In the back, far from the paths maintained for mourners of the recent dead, is the crypt of the ancient queens: the First Crypt. They leave you in front of a stair, roughly hewn into weathered jade stone, which passes steeply up to a massive facade, an entryway, and statues looming over you. Cold air wafts slowly down the steps to your feet.

Choice.text: Climb the steps and enter the crypt

Page.Title: The worn panel
Page.Text: Carefully inspecting the south wall, you find one panel is different from the others, its sconce empty of oil and the engraved snake face worn down from repeated touch.

Page.Title: Cutting the web
Page.Text: You slash through the web of strings, leaving them all hanging loose from their nails as you carve paths through the room. As you finish, you hear a hiss as the room fills with a gas, apparently triggered by the strings.

Choice.text: Hold your breath and endure it

Page.Title: Clean through the neck
Page.Text: With a lucky blow, you cut clean through the snake's neck, its head tumbling into the pool with a splash, followed quickly by its body.

Choice.text: Stand and look at the water

Page.Title: Fangs
Page.Text: The snake digs its fangs deep into you, and the wound goes cold almost at once. The venom does its work in a rush rather than over hours, and what it leaves behind stays in your blood.

Page.Title: The serpent in the pool
Page.Text: A massive emerald serpent emerges from the pool with a burst of energy, spraying the room with water.

Page.Title: The faun and the pool
Page.Text: At the end of a short hallway is a small grotto in the wall. A statue of a faun pours a dark liquid into a pool around its feet.

Text.Content: Gaps in the stones of the back wall of the grotto allow points of light through, suggesting there is another room on the other side. It appears you could try to move some of the stones to make a passage, but it would be difficult to do so quietly.
Stones have been moved from the wall behind the statue to create a passageway to the west.

Choice.text: Try to move the stones quietly

Page.Title: Over, under, around
Page.Text: You work your way carefully over, under and around the intertwining body of the stone snake. It is slow work. You do not recall your exact path, and you will have to spend the same amount of time the next time you move through this room.

Choice.text: Come out in the far corner of the hall

Page.Title: You hold your breath
Page.Text: You feel drowsiness beginning to overtake you, but you harden your will and hold your breath. In a few moments the gas dissipates and you find you can breathe safely again.

Page.Title: Light along the walls
Page.Text: You light the oil in the sconces one by one, filling the room with light and warmth. You find that one sconce on the south wall is empty, and it is immediately apparent that the engravings on this panel are different from the others, the snake's face worn down by repeated touch.

Page.Title: Dust and nothing
Page.Text: You search, but are unable to find anything significant along the south wall, as dust blown on the wind fills your eyes and makes you cough.

Page.Title: Warm water
Page.Text: The water is warm but surprisingly refreshing, soothing your throat as it goes down. You could fill the crystal vial on the table and have the same comfort later.

Choice.text: Fill the vial and take it with you
Leave the vial where it is

Page.Title: Round on yourself
Page.Text: Try as you might, you cannot make heads or tails of how to go through this snake. The coils bring you round on yourself, and you eventually find yourself back where you started.

Choice.text: Stand again at the eastern entrance
Stand again in the far corner

Page.Title: Sleep, and a wooden cage
Page.Text: You feel drowsiness rushing upon you. Although you fight back, you are unable to keep it up, and you soon fall asleep. When you wake up you find yourself locked in a wooden cage, the smell of death and roasting meat filling your nose before your eyes clear and you can see the room.

Choice.text: Wait to see what they want

Page.Title: The engraved room
Page.Text: You are in a large room, fifty feet square. There are double doors on the north wall and a single door on the west wall. The walls are covered in elaborate engraved images, and every ten feet along them stands a bronze sconce.

Text.Content: There is no light source, and an odd draft blowing in from the south wall suggests there may be a hidden door in that area.
The sconces you lit burn steadily, and the room is bright and warm.
The panel on the south wall stands open where you touched the snake, a secret door onto a dark passage.

Choice.text: Go north through the double doors
Go west through the single door
Go south through the secret door

Page.Title: Through the holes in the web
Page.Text: You carefully slide your body through the holes in the web without touching a string. Now that you have done it once, you think you could do it again if you take your time.

Page.Title: The pool, and what floats in it
Page.Text: You stand by the pool, now tinged red with blood from the snake corpse floating on its surface. Inspecting the water more closely, you can see it is not, in fact, emerald, but normal clear water.

Choice.text: Go back to the entrance of the chamber

Page.Title: Snakes, and rabbits bowing
Page.Text: The imagery is made up of ten-foot panels, each showing massive snakes in various positions and crowds of rabbits apparently bowing down in worship to them. Each and every one of the snakes is defaced save for one, which appears instead to be worn down from repeated touch.

Page.Title: Inside the serpent
Page.Text: You push through the cramped tunnel and find that inside it is much less complicated than it appears from the outside. Rather than twists and turns, it takes you on a relatively straight path north, opening up into a new chamber.

Page.Title: The panel swings inward
Page.Text: When you touch the snake head, the panel slowly swings inward, revealing a secret door on the south wall.

Page.Title: The thread holds
Page.Text: You work your way carefully over, under and around the intertwining body of the snake. It is slow work, but the yarn magically strings itself out as you go, marking a quick path through the statue.

Choice.text: Come out in the far corner of the hall

Page.Title: A shadow under the surface
Page.Text: As you look more carefully, you see a long dark shadow swirling around under the surface of the water. Whatever it is has not noticed you.

Choice.text: Back off while you still can
Try to get the water anyway

Page.Title: The far corner of the hall
Page.Text: In the south-west corner of the hall are two sets of double doors, one on the south wall and one on the west wall. Behind you the jade coils stand between you and the daylight of the entrance.

Text.Content: Your white thread comes out of the coils here, and runs back the way you came.

Choice.text: Go south through the double doors
Go west through the double doors
Follow the white thread back to the entrance

Page.Title: The green chamber
Page.Text: You are in the entrance of a large round chamber, fifty feet across, lit in a hazy green light from a rough gemstone in the ceiling. Fog fills the room from a large pool of water covering much of the floor. It is impossible to tell if the water itself is green or if it is a trick of the light. Near the edge of the water, a small stone table has a crystal vial on it.

Choice.text: Look at what floats in the pool
Go back to the hall of the statue

Page.Title: A string catches your foot
Page.Text: Moving carefully through the web of strings, you misstep and your foot catches and pulls a string. You hear a hiss as the room fills with a gas, apparently triggered by the strings.

Choice.text: Hold your breath and endure it

Page.Title: The vial, and what came out of the water
Page.Text: You quickly fill the vial with water and jump back as a massive snake emerges. When you have time to inspect the vial, you will find the water in it is clear, not emerald. You have enough time to flee the room.

Choice.text: Flee to the hall of the statue

Page.Title: The king of the rabets
Page.Text: After a time, a rabet opens the cage and grabs you by the hand to lead you to their king. You learn this one can speak common, although the others speak only in low barks and growls. Acting as a translator for their king, you learn that they want a snake egg from a nearby room. If you retrieve it for them, they will reward you with treasure. They provide a map of nearby rooms with the egg room marked with an X.

Choice.text: Take the map and stand up

Page.Title: The stones give way
Page.Text: You manage to quietly move enough of the stones to make a passage you can crawl through.

Page.Title: The gas thins out
Page.Text: You feel drowsiness beginning to overtake you, but you harden your will and hold your breath. In a few moments the gas dissipates and you find you can breathe safely again. The web hangs loose now, sprung: it will not catch anyone twice.

Page.Title: The hall of the jade serpent
Page.Text:
You stand at the entrance on the east side of a large hall, sixty feet by fifty, lit faintly with light from the opening to the outside. The space is full, wall to wall and floor to ceiling, with an enormous jade statue of a snake, twisting and turning over itself, tying itself in knots, but with space enough to move through them.
The head of the snake is to your right, mouth open, large pointed fangs ready to strike. Behind the fangs, it appears there is a tunnel inside of the snake.

Text.Content: At your feet is a skein of pure white yarn, glowing with a slightly magical aura.
A white thread runs away from your feet and disappears among the coils. You laid it yourself, and it still marks the way through.
The bottle at your belt is full of emerald water, and the daylight is behind you.

Choice.text: Walk out of the crypt with the water
Climb into the mouth and follow the tunnel inside the snake
Follow the white thread to the far corner
Work around the coils, unspooling the yarn behind you
Work around the coils with nothing but your hands

Page.Title: You died
Page.Text: You died in the First Crypt. The magic scroll returns to the castle on its own, carrying your notes and your map. Future adventurers may find your body, and take anything you were carrying.

Choice.text: Take a new volunteer from the court and begin again

Page.Title: The rabet room, from the north-west
Page.Text: You are at the entrance in the north-west corner of a very large room, a hundred feet by forty.

Text.Content: The room is full of lanky armoured creatures with pointed faces and tall floppy ears. They move about in the flickering light of a bonfire in the centre of the room, where they are roasting portions of a giant snake. You recognise the creatures as rabets, tricksters known for their cunning ambushes and traps underground.
As you realise this, the two guards flanking this passageway notice you.
The two guards you killed lie in the shadows on either side of the entrance, and nobody has moved them.
You know there is a secret door in the north-east corner.
Rabets lie dead about the room. Portions of giant snake are burning to a crisp over the bonfire in the centre, and nobody is turning them.
The room is full of barking and the smell of roasted snake. They do not care that you pass through, but they do not want you close to them either.

Choice.text: Go north to the small room
Go through the secret door in the north-east corner
Announce yourself and deal with the rabets
Slip along the north wall to the secret door
Slip along the north wall to the north-east corner

Page.Title: The room of strings
Page.Text: You are in a small room, twenty feet square. A short hallway to the east leads to a single door. There is an open passageway to the south. A short hallway to the west dead ends at a grotto, from which you can hear the sound of trickling water.

Text.Content: The room is filled with an intricate web of strings tied off to nails on the floor, ceiling and walls. There is just enough space to squeeze between the strings in some places, but only barely.
Since you have been through the web before, you remember your path and how to cross safely if you take your time.
Strings dangle from the walls and ceiling where you cut them.
The web of strings hangs loose, sprung: you do not think it poses a danger any more.

Choice.text: Go east to the single door
Pick your remembered way east to the single door
Pick your remembered way west to the grotto
Attempt to move through the strings

Page.Title: A clang in the wrong room
Page.Text: Attempting to move quietly through the space you misstep, and a clang echoes through the room as your backpack falls to the ground. In a moment you are rushed by ten rabets and their king.

Page.Title: Along the north wall
Page.Text: You move unnoticed along the north wall of the room. You realise quickly it is the only safe area outside the view of the rabets moving about the middle and southern parts of the room. As you near the passageway in the north-west corner, you see it is flanked by guards hiding in the shadows.

Choice.text: Try to find a nonviolent way into the passage
Go back to the secret door

Page.Title: Speaking with the rabets
Page.Text: You put your hands where they can see them.

Text.Content: The rabets are surprised at first, raising their weapons. But when they see you are an adventurer, one rushes forward and grabs you by the hand to lead you to their king. You learn this one can speak common, although the others speak only in low barks and growls. Acting as a translator for their king, you learn that they want a snake egg from a nearby room. If you retrieve it for them, they will reward you with treasure. They provide a map of nearby rooms with the egg room marked with an X.

The rabets break out in celebration when they see the egg, howling with delight. King Rabet holds out his arms to take it, while his translator holds out a small sack to you. Inside the sack are five gems. The translator explains that they will not bother you if you come to this room again, but they do not want anything else to do with you. Frankly, they do not like your smell. Turns out rabets can be really hurtful.

Choice.text: Take the map and turn back to the room
Hand over the egg and take the sack

Page.Title: The stone on your foot
Page.Text: As you are moving the final stone to create a passage, you drop it on your foot and let out a loud scream. A moment later, something appears in the passage you have created.

Choice.text: Turn to face whatever is coming

Page.Title: The two guards
Page.Text: You are fighting the two rabet guards who flank the passageway. If the fight lasts, the room will hear it.

Page.Title: A blow to the back of the head
Page.Text: With a thud, a blunt object smacks the back of your head and you are knocked out. When you wake up you find yourself locked in a wooden cage, the smell of death and roasting meat filling your nose before your eyes clear and you can see the room.

Choice.text: Wait to see what they want

Page.Title: The north-east corner
Page.Text: You move unnoticed along the north wall of the room, and soon arrive at the passage in the north-east corner, where you find there is a secret door on the wall.

Page.Title: The room seen through the secret door
Page.Text: You are at the secret door in the north-east corner of a very large room, a hundred feet by forty.

Text.Content: The room is full of lanky armoured creatures with pointed faces and tall floppy ears, moving about in the flickering light of a bonfire in the centre, where they are roasting portions of a giant snake. They have not yet noticed you as you look through the door. There is another open passageway in the north-west corner.
Nobody in the room is watching this door any more.

Choice.text: Go back into the engraved room
Try to move unnoticed through the room

Page.Title: The room hears the fight
Page.Text: Hearing the clamour of your fight, eight more rabets and their king rush over to join in.

Page.Title: Dark water from the faun
Page.Text: It is normal water, refreshing but unremarkable. You refill your waterskin.

Choice.text: Straighten up and look around the grotto

Page.Title: The long hallway
Page.Text: You are in a hallway, ten feet wide and eighty long. There are doors to the east, south, west and north.

Page.Title: The L-shaped hallway
Page.Text: A long L-shaped hallway opens into a room at the south end and a cavern at the north end.

Page.Title: The guards are down
Page.Text: The two guards lie in the shadows on either side of the entrance, and for the moment nobody in the room has looked this way.

Page.Title: The room of pyres
Page.Text: You are in a room, sixty feet by forty, dominated by a green stone platform filling most of the floor. Partially burnt wood, ash and bone on the platform indicate it is a place for funeral pyres. The edges of the room are filled with rows of jade urns. One stands next to the platform, partially full of ash, the burnt corpse of a woman in green robes beside it. You may take the robes; you find nothing else of value if you search her.

Choice.text: Take the green robes and go east

Page.Title: The cavern, north bank
Page.Text: You are in a large, natural cavern, walls of rough green stone, much unlike the finely carved chambers of the crypt. A river of emerald water rushes through the centre of the cavern, running from a hole in the north-east wall down to the south-west. It would be impossible to cross safely. On the far side of the stream are rows upon rows of jade jars, neatly arranged.

Page.Title: The camp, gone quiet
Page.Text: The last of them stops moving. Portions of giant snake go on burning to a crisp over the bonfire in the centre, and there is nobody left to turn them.

Page.Title: The room of hot mud
Page.Text: A large room, ninety feet by forty, is full of a thick bed of hot mud, steam rising and filling the air, lit by large glowing eggs in clusters throughout the space.

Page.Title: The room of the purple snake
Page.Text: You are in a dark room, forty feet by fifty.

Text.Content: A massive purple snake is curled up sleeping in the northern half of the room. Reaching either exit would mean moving quietly past it.
The massive purple snake lies dead, rotting on top of a pile of treasure. The stench of its death ichor is so strong you cannot stay in here long without succumbing and passing out.
There is a secret passage in the south-east corner, the one you opened from the grotto.

Choice.text: Go west to the room of pyres
Move quietly west to the room of pyres
Look for a way to kill the snake
Quickly grab treasure before moving on

Page.Title: Bones, rags and ash
Page.Text: Among the snake bones, filthy rags and ash piles of the rabet encampment, you find a thousand coins and five purple gems.

Page.Title: The vines
Page.Text: A vine lashes out and wraps around your leg, burning your skin where it touches, before you can take an egg. There are four of them, and they move together.

Page.Title: An egg, and a jump backwards
Page.Text: You snatch an egg and jump back out of the reach of the vines. It takes both arms to carry.

Page.Title: The shifting maze
Page.Text: In a large room, sixty feet square, panels of jade stone form a constantly shifting maze, panels rising and falling from the floor rhythmically, the pattern of the maze changing with each motion. There are passages at the east and west ends of the room.

Choice.text: Work your way through the maze to the east
Work your way through the maze to the west

Page.Title: The emerald water
Page.Text: The emerald water is healing. The ache goes out of you as you swallow, and whatever was in your blood is not in it any more.

Choice.text: Stand up on the north bank
Stand up on the south bank

Page.Title: The egg cluster
Page.Text: Six large glowing eggs are clustered together in a nest of neon orange vines. As you look, you see the vines are slowly moving on their own around the eggs. With care, you could take an egg, but it would require both arms to carry it.

Page.Title: The vines in pieces
Page.Text: The vines lie in pieces, steam rising more strongly from the orange liquid that flows out of them. You can take an egg now, at your leisure.

Choice.text: Take an egg and step back

Page.Title: It divides
Page.Text: Your strike causes a smaller pudding to divide from the main blob. There are two of them now, and the small one is quicker.

Page.Title: Through the maze
Page.Text: You manage to pass safely through the maze. Along the way you find a purse dropped by a previous adventurer.

Text.Content: You already took what was in it; the leather lies where you dropped it.

Choice.text: Take the purse and go out to the east
Take the purse and go out to the west

Page.Title: The water, close up
Page.Text: On inspection, you can see the water is pure emerald in colour, exactly like that you were sent to find. An empty bottle lies in the sand on the bank.

Page.Title: The cavern, south bank
Page.Text: You are in a large, natural cavern, walls of rough green stone, much unlike the finely carved chambers of the crypt. A river of emerald water rushes through the centre, running from a hole in the north-east wall down to the west. It would be impossible to cross safely. On the far side of the stream are rows upon rows of jade jars, neatly arranged.

Choice.text: Collect some water in the bottle

Page.Title: An egg, quietly
Page.Text: You grab an egg without being caught by the vines, which lash out at you as you pull away.

Page.Title: The room of hot tubs
Page.Text: You are in a room, sixty feet by forty, full of steam and dimly lit cracks in the tiled floor, under which fires appear to be burning. Marble tubs of hot water are arranged in two rows down the middle. This would be a nice place to rest, but there appears to be nothing else of interest here.

Page.Title: Absorbed
Page.Text: As you die, you are absorbed by the pudding. Except for the magic scroll, which returns to the castle, your inventory is retrievable by future adventurers only if they defeat the pudding.

Choice.text: Take a new volunteer from the court and begin again

Page.Title: The emerald pudding
Page.Text: The blob comes on, and where it touches, it takes. You could keep swinging your own weapons, or reach for the torch with the jade handle at your feet.

Page.Title: The ring in the goo
Page.Text: With a final blow of the torch, the pudding goes up in flames, soon leaving only a pile of burnt goo on the floor. Nearly hidden in the goo, you find a gold ring set with a large emerald. The door has reappeared.

Choice.text: Take the ring and leave the room

Page.Title: The head among the coils
Page.Text: You find the snake's head amongst its coiled body. A strike from a big enough hand-to-hand weapon would be enough to kill it here.

Choice.text: Try to kill the snake where it sleeps

Page.Title: What you can carry, quickly
Page.Text: You are able to collect a handful of coins, but staying longer would make you pass out from the stench of death. You could perhaps try again the next time you pass through this room.

Page.Title: "I accept this offering"
Page.Text: As you cross the circle of the candles, a disembodied, deep, raspy voice says: "I accept this offering." The candles flame high, scorching the ceiling. You turn and see the door you entered through is no longer there, only a smooth green wall. The pool congeals and rises up into an amorphous emerald blob lumbering toward you. At your feet you notice a torch with a jade handle.

Page.Title: A mighty blow
Page.Text: With a mighty blow you kill the snake. It begins to let out a putrid odour as ichor flows from its death wound.

Page.Title: What it sleeps on
Page.Text: You find the snake is sleeping on top of a pile of treasure. With luck you could gather some of it without waking it.

Page.Title: As much as you dare
Page.Text: You are able to collect a handful of coins, but you fear any more would wake the snake from the way it is beginning to squirm. You could perhaps try again later, when it has settled.

Page.Title: The jade torch
Page.Text: You take up the torch with the jade handle. It burns hotter than it should, and the blob flinches from the light before you have even swung it.

Enemy.name: An emerald pudding, shrinking from the flame

Page.Title: The room of black candles
Page.Text: In a large, semi-rounded room, sixty feet across, jade crystal formations serve as candlestands for smoky black candles.

Text.Content: They stand around a pool of dark green liquid.
They stand around smears of black goo burnt on the floor. There is nothing of interest here now.

Page.Title: Not enough to kill it
Page.Text: You strike a blow, but it is not enough to kill the snake outright. It comes awake around your arm.

Page.Title: The purple snake, awake
Page.Text: The snake is awake and it has seen you. Its bite carries a venom that works fast.

Page.Title: A panel rises
Page.Text: You misstep and are knocked by a panel rising from the floor.

Choice.text: Pick yourself up and try again

Page.Title: The brood
Page.Text: As you dip the bottle to fill it, a brood of five snakes jumps out of the water, forcing you back, and then moves to attack you.

Page.Title: The bottle fills
Page.Text: You hold the bottle under the surface until it is full, and stopper it. The water inside it is the colour of the river, and it does not fade.

Page.Title: With the snakes gone
Page.Text: With the snakes gone, you may safely collect a bottle of water. It is the colour of the river, and it does not fade.

Page.Title: Swept away
Page.Text: Swooning from the snakebites, you fall into the water and are swept away. The water heals you as you float through a dark tunnel, and a moment later you wash up on the bank in another cavern.

Choice.text: Get to your feet on the far bank

Page.Title: Out of the cavern
Page.Text:
When you emerge from the cavern, guards meet you on the steps. One takes the bottle of water and mounts a horse, rushing off back to the castle. Another hands you a bag with five thousand coins and a letter releasing you from service to the king.
You are free to pursue further adventures, if you dare.

Page.Title: Four rabets, and a dead snake
Page.Text: Four rabets come round the corner dragging a dead snake by the tail. They stop when they see you. The one at the front lets go of the tail, and the body slaps against the stone.

Enemy.name: Four rabets dragging a dead snake

Page.Title: Hunting
Page.Text: You hear them before you see them: five snakes moving fast and low over the stone, spread out the way things spread out when they are hunting together.

Enemy.name: A pack of five hunting snakes

Page.Title: Two rabets, lost
Page.Text: Two rabets come round the corner arguing in low barks, and stop dead. They are not where they meant to be, and neither of them expected you.

Page.Title: A snake taking a nap
Page.Text: A snake lies coiled in a hollow of the stone, out of the draught, asleep. You could try to get past it. It might not stay asleep.

Page.Title: Two parties at once
Page.Text: Four rabets come round the corner with a dead snake, and behind them, drawn by the noise, four more. Nobody backs off.

Enemy.name: Four rabets dragging a dead snake
Four more rabets, drawn by the noise

Page.Title: Hunters and hunted, both here
Page.Text: Four rabets are dragging their dead snake past you when the pack that has been following the smell arrives. For a moment nobody is sure who is fighting whom. The moment passes.

Enemy.name: Four rabets dragging a dead snake
A pack of five hunting snakes

Page.Title: The party and the strays
Page.Text: Four rabets with a dead snake, and two more who have clearly been looking for them. Finding you first does not improve anybody's temper.

Enemy.name: Four rabets dragging a dead snake

Page.Title: Enough noise to wake it
Page.Text: Four rabets come round the corner dragging a dead snake. They are not quiet about it, and in a hollow above you something that was asleep stops being asleep.

Enemy.name: Four rabets dragging a dead snake

Page.Title: Two packs, one corridor of stone
Page.Text: Snakes come from both sides at once. They are not hunting each other, which leaves only you.

Enemy.name: A pack of five hunting snakes
A second pack, coming the other way

Page.Title: The strays run into the pack
Page.Text: Two lost rabets come round the corner at a trot, see you, and stop. Behind them the hunting pack that has been herding them all along arrives.

Enemy.name: A pack of five hunting snakes

Page.Title: The pack, and what it wakes
Page.Text: The hunting pack pours over the stone, and the noise brings the sleeper out of its hollow behind you.

Enemy.name: A pack of five hunting snakes

Page.Title: Four rabets, none of whom know the way
Page.Text: Two rabets come round one corner, and two more from the other side, all of them lost, all of them relieved to see somebody until they see it is you.

Page.Title: They step on it before you do
Page.Text: Two lost rabets come round the corner at a bad angle and one of them puts a foot in the hollow where a snake is sleeping. Now none of you have a choice.

Page.Title: Two hollows, two sleepers
Page.Text: There is a snake asleep in a hollow ahead of you and another behind, and the stone carries every sound you make to both of them.

Page.Title: You can go on
Page.Text: When it is over you stand still for a while, listening. Nothing else moves. You pick up where you left off.

Choice.text: Come out in the far corner of the hall
Come out beside the entrance of the hall
